title: Resident Trust Fund Accounts: Returning Transfers That Paid Payer-Covered Ancillary Items
content:
## Policy

When the resident's payer covers an item or service on the ancillary account that a transfer from this account paid, the improper part of that transfer is returned to the account with the reason payer-covered item, naming the transfer, within the improper charge reversal business days.

This applies to every Resident Trust Fund Accounts tier. The ancillary account is the resident's account under Ancillary and Optional Services Billing; the transfer is a bill transfer from the resident funds account to a charge on that ancillary account.

## Business effect

The return is one entry on the resident funds account's ledger. It names the transfer being given back and the reason it was improper, is dated the day it is processed, and raises the account balance by the amount returned; every later lookup of the account shows the higher balance.

## Recording the return: `return_improper_transfer_e2970e4f`

This is an agent-side tool. It is not in the default tool list: unlock it first, then call it.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `trust_account_id` | the reference number of the resident funds account the money goes back into, as shown on the account record | identifier |
| `withdrawal_entry_id` | the reference number of the transfer entry being given back, as shown on that entry's line in the account's ledger | identifier |
| `reversal_reason` | why the transfer was improper | one of the four values below |
| `amount` | the money returned to the account | US dollars, a positive decimal number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent, no currency sign |

Values of `reversal_reason`:
- `payer_covered_item` — it paid for an item or service that Medicare or Medical Assistance covers;
- `unauthorized` — it was made without the written authority the account requires;
- `duplicate` — it repeated a ledger entry that paid the same thing;
- `amount_error` — it was made for the wrong amount.

**Return.** A one-line confirmation of the form "Returned <amount> USD to account <account> for entry <transfer entry> (<reason>) as entry <new entry>; new balance <balance> USD." The presence of the new entry's reference number shows that the return was recorded.

## Contract Q&A

**Does the tool work out the amount?** No. It records the amount it is given, rounded half up to the cent, as a positive figure.

**What does the resident see?** A credit line for the return on the account, and a higher balance.
